message.content: Forty-two is still well under North Carolina’s mortgage value, so I’ll keep the minimum raise and the green block.
message.reasoning:
I need to decide on a bid for North Carolina Avenue in the auction.

I have $726 and one Get Out of Jail Free card. The auction is at $41 with p4 as the high bidder. I will bid $42 to win under the $150 mortgage value. This nets cash and blocks p4 from a PA+NC pair.

Mortgaging immediately after purchase yields $108 cash back, making this a clear profit. I am now weighing the risks.

Cash drops to $684 after the bid. I can mortgage North Carolina immediately upon acquisition, before my next roll. The worst-case rent from Pennsylvania Avenue is $1700 for Boardwalk with four houses, but that would occur on a future turn.

I am now unsure whether mortgaging is allowed between turns. If it is not, the $42 bid simply reduces cash until my next turn. That is acceptable because the $726 buffer easily absorbs the loss. Even without immediate mortgage, the bid still blocks p4 from completing a green set.

p4 has $763 and is incrementing by $1. I will keep bidding $42 to stay below the $150 cap.

I now suspect p4 is also planning to mortgage North Carolina for $150. If so, the rational bid is up to $149. I will raise to $150 to secure the property and block p4 from completing a green set.

Blocking p4 from a second green is less valuable than it first appeared. Pacific Avenue is mortgaged by p1, so they cannot complete the set without trading.

If p4 wins and mortgages North Carolina, they still lose $150 net. The same arbitrage applies to both players.

The real question is whether to spend $150 now or let p4 spend it. p4 is in jail with light blues and unmortgaged railroads. That makes them more dangerous if they land on those spaces.

p1 is nearly broke with only $29 and heavily built dark blues. They might sell Pacific Avenue to p4 if p4 can pay. That would let p4 complete the green set later. This makes blocking p4 from North Carolina more valuable than it first appeared.
